theses.blurb: The thesis weakened this week, with health moving from 0.00 to -0.20. The H20 export ban delivered an $8B revenue hit and effectively ended Nvidia's Hopper data-center business in China, while Q2 results flagged a slowdown in Data Center growth that analysts warn could extend into 2026. Market share erosion is also becoming harder to dismiss — Nvidia's AI accelerator share is projected to fall from ~87% to ~70-75% by 2026, and landmark deals like Anthropic committing to one million Google TPUs and Meta in talks for multi-billion-dollar TPU deployments signal that custom ASICs are making real inroads. Compounding the pressure, Tencent's capex is already declining, Michael Burry's SBC and depreciation critique rattled enough investors that Nvidia felt compelled to push back directly, and broader market skepticism about the durability of AI infrastructure spending and Nvidia's exceptional margins is visibly rising.
